questions.question: In the water-pipe picture of a circuit, what do voltage and current correspond to?
questions.answer: Voltage is the water pressure (the push); current is the amount of water flowing.
questions.hint: One is a push, the other is a flow.

questions.question: Why does a circuit need a path back to ground, and what happens if the loop is broken?
questions.answer: Current flows only around a complete loop from the power source through the part and back to ground. If the loop is broken, nothing flows and the part stays off.
questions.hint: Think of the pipe that returns water to the pump.

questions.question: What is a GPIO pin and what two modes did we use?
questions.answer: A General Purpose Input/Output pin the program can control. It can be an output (the board sets it HIGH or LOW) or an input (the board reads it).
questions.hint: The program decides which direction it faces.

questions.question: A sketch calls digitalWrite(4, HIGH) but never calls pinMode(4, OUTPUT). What is the safe expectation?
questions.answer: You cannot count on the LED lighting; the pin was never set up as an output, so always call pinMode first.
questions.hint: Which step tells the pin which way to face?

questions.question: Put these in order and say what each does: upload, compile, write.
questions.answer: Write the sketch; compile turns it into machine code and catches typos; upload sends the machine code to the board's memory.
questions.hint: The computer translates before it sends.

questions.question: Upload fails with 'Failed to connect to ESP32: Wrong boot mode'. Name two things to try.
questions.answer: Check the USB cable carries data, choose the right port, and hold the BOOT button while upload starts.

questions.question: Your LED on pin 4 lights but is very dim and the pin is hot. What component did you likely forget and why does it matter?
questions.answer: The current-limiting resistor (about 220 ohm). Without it too much current flows and can damage the LED or the pin.
